Yom Kippur Observances and Road Safety Concerns

Yom Kippur, the holiest day in Judaism, began on September 20. Observances focus on atonement, forgiveness, and inner reflection. The holiday is traditionally marked by fasting and prayer. In past years, road accidents have occurred during the Yom Kippur period, with six fatalities reported over the last decade. The observance encourages participants to "go, eat with joy" after the period of reflection and atonement.
